drug_class: Adrenal steroid synthesis inhibitor (diagnostic agent / therapeutic agent)
purpose: Metyrapone is used mainly as a test to check how well your pituitary gland and adrenal glands are working together. It can also be used to treat certain conditions where your body makes too much of a stress hormone called cortisol, such as Cushing's syndrome. Your doctor may use it short-term to help control high cortisol levels before surgery or other treatments.
how_it_works: Your adrenal glands normally make a hormone called cortisol, which helps your body handle stress. Metyrapone works by blocking a specific enzyme in the adrenal glands that is needed to produce cortisol. When cortisol production is blocked, your pituitary gland responds by releasing more of another hormone called ACTH, which doctors can measure to evaluate how well your hormone system is working.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, low blood pressure, and feeling lightheaded when you stand up. Some people may also feel unusually tired or have mild skin rash. These effects are usually manageable, but let your doctor know if they bother you.
warnings: This medication can cause your cortisol levels to drop too low, which is dangerous — watch for signs like severe weakness, confusion, low blood pressure, or extreme fatigue and seek emergency care right away if these occur. It should be used very carefully in people with adrenal insufficiency. Pregnant women should not use this medication as it can harm the baby. Always take it with food to reduce stomach upset, and never stop it suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: For the diagnostic test, a common adult dose is 750 mg by mouth every 4 hours for 6 doses (a total of 4.5 grams over one day). For treating high cortisol conditions, dosing is individualized by your doctor, often ranging from 250 mg to 6 grams per day divided into several doses, adjusted based on your lab results. Always take it with food or milk to help prevent an upset stomach.
